chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Ibrāhīm claims that the diyah of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian is equal. So he said: “Yes, he spoke the truth.”

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian; here, a non-Muslim whose diyah is being compared
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth; the correct legal statement as affirmed by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيِّ: a Magian; here, included among the non-Muslim groups whose diyah is addressed
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew; here, one of the protected non-Muslim groups discussed in legal rulings
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money; the financial compensation due in cases of unlawful killing or injury
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ: equal; having the same legal amount or status in this ruling

ai.seo_question: Is the diyah of a Jew, Christian, and Magian considered equal in this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirmed the correctness of the statement that the diyah of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is the same. It belongs to the legal discussion of retaliation and blood-money between different religious and social groups.
